subject.title: [Feature]: Compaction: configurable model override + flush-then-reset mode

question: Should OpenClaw add a compaction-threshold flush-then-reset policy now that compaction.model and memoryFlush.model are shipped, and what privacy/provider/session-state semantics should govern it?
rationale: Source inspection can prove the remaining feature is absent, but automation should not choose whether a silent memory write is sufficient to discard active session context or how that model/provider routing should be governed.

options.title: Design unified reset-memory policy first
options.body: Keep this issue open and align compaction-threshold reset mode with reset-time memory work so explicit, daily, idle, and compaction-pressure resets share one bounded policy.

options.title: Add default-off resetAfterFlush
options.body: Approve a narrow opt-in mode with explicit success criteria, provider/auth behavior, timeout, notification, and regression proof requirements.

options.title: Reject automatic reset after flush
options.body: Keep compaction as the canonical context-preservation path and rely on model overrides, memory flush, and manual reset flows for cost control.

recommendation.title: Design unified reset-memory policy first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and align compaction-threshold reset mode with reset-time memory work so explicit, daily, idle, and compaction-pressure resets share one bounded policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across pre-compaction memory flush, memoryFlush.model, and reset-adjacent runtime behavior.
